title: Spanish preterite for completed events in conversation
snippet: Use the preterite for completed actions with a clear end in Spanish conversation.
content:
The preterite narrates completed actions with a clear end point, such as ayer, el sábado or anoche. Example: Ayer hablé con mi hermana. Practice: Complete: Anoche nosotros ___ en un restaurante. (cenar) Answer: cenamos.

Irregular preterite forms like fui, hice and tuve are frequent in finished actions. Example: El verano pasado fui a México.

title: Spanish imperfect for descriptions and habits in conversation
snippet: Use the imperfect for habits, descriptions and background in Spanish conversation.
content:
The imperfect describes habits and repeated past actions, often with siempre or todos los días. Example: De niño jugaba en el parque todos los días. Practice: Complete: Cuando vivía en Madrid, ___ en metro. (viajar, yo) Answer: viajaba.

The imperfect also gives descriptions of people, weather and time in the past. Example: Era tarde y hacía frío.

title: Expressing opinions in Spanish conversation
snippet: Creo que, pienso que and me parece que introduce opinions in Spanish conversation.
content:
To give opinions, use creo que, pienso que or me parece que followed by the indicative. Example: Creo que la película es muy buena. Practice: Complete: ___ que el libro es interesante. (creer, yo) Answer: creo.

To ask for opinions, use ¿qué piensas de...? or ¿qué te parece...? Example: ¿Qué te parece el plan?

title: Preterite and imperfect together in storytelling
snippet: Contrast the imperfect scene with preterite events when telling a story in Spanish.
content:
In storytelling the imperfect sets the scene and the preterite tells what happened next, the contrasting events of the story. Example: Llovía cuando llegué a casa. Practice: Complete: Mientras yo leía, ___ el teléfono. (sonar) Answer: sonó.

Background versus events: interrupted actions use the imperfect for the background and the preterite for the interruption in a story. Example: Dormía cuando sonó la alarma.

title: Disagreeing with no creo que and the subjunctive
snippet: Negated opinions such as no creo que take the subjunctive in Spanish.
content:
Disagreeing with negated opinions: after no creo que or no pienso que, the verb takes the subjunctive. Example: No creo que sea verdad. Practice: Complete: No pienso que ella ___ razón. (tener) Answer: tenga.

Subjunctive forms after negated verbs of opinion express doubt or disagreeing politely. Example: No me parece que sea buena idea.
